name: Padmāvatī Devī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Śrī Rohiṇī**, Vasudeva's wife, the mother of Balarāma, who lives in Nanda's house in Gokula with Yaśodā like the Gaṅgā with the Yamunā.

## Gopāla-campū — Rohiṇī

- **Her coming to Vraja** (Pūrva-campū 3.80–81): «Vasudeva, disturbed by uncontrollable Kaṃsa's anger, sent Rohiṇī, favorable to Vraja, to Vraja. Riding on a horse, she arrived secretly. She was very faithful to her husband. Just on seeing her, Nanda's assembly became joyful… Yaśodā and Rohiṇī, like the Yamunā and Gaṅgā Rivers, became overcome with bliss on meeting and showered bliss on each other and everyone else.» «Understanding that, starting with Jyeṣṭha month, Rohiṇī was pregnant for three months, Yaśodā, identifying with her, became most joyful.»
- **Balarāma's birth** (Pūrva-campū 3.86, verse 26): «Yogamāyā then destroyed the seven-month embryo in Rohiṇī's womb and transferred the seventh month embryo from Devakī's womb. After the fourteenth month of pregnancy… during Śravaṇa constellation, Rohiṇī, in great joy gave birth to a most beautiful son… She was a she-elephant giving birth to an elephant calf endowed with evident prowess. She was a lotus giving birth to a white lotus.» «Rohiṇī gave birth to Balarāma, whose face was like the moon… whose complexion was like a white autumn cloud.»
- **Mother of Kṛṣṇa too**: «As a cow meets her calf, Yaśodā met Kṛṣṇa. As a cow has affection for her calf, all the people saw Rohiṇī displaying affection for Kṛṣṇa»; «Kṛṣṇa offered respects to the lotus feet of Yaśodā and Rohiṇī» (Pūrva-campū 2.24–25). «Though stunned and weeping, Yaśodā applied tilaka on Kṛṣṇa, but without the help of Rohiṇī, she would not be able to do this» (2, verse 13). «Rohiṇī, thinking of his safety, said to Kṛṣṇa, “O child whose mother is Yaśodā! Your mother has raised you from childhood and thus you do not respect her orders. But do not disobey my orders”» (2.62).
- **Her love for Rādhā** (Pūrva-campū 2.15): «Rohiṇī spoke: “O Yaśodā! The constellation Rohiṇī, bestowing all happiness, has come today. Give her the order. She is more skillful than all other women with good qualities… Lalitā and others are her expansions.”»
- **In Goloka** (Pūrva-campū 1.70): in Nanda's palace «To the north Rohiṇī lives, overcome by fresh bliss».

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 1.70, 2.13, 2.15, 2.24–25, 2.62, 3.80–86 (verse 26).

name: Hāḍāi Paṇḍita
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Vasudeva**, son of Śūra and grandson of Devamiḍha, the father of Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa; cousin and friend of Nanda, whose father Parjanya was Śūra's brother.

## Gopāla-campū — Vasudeva

- **His family** (Pūrva-campū 3.19): «Devamiḍha, who personified all the best qualities of the Yadu dynasty… had two wives. One was of kṣatriya family and the other was of vaiśya family. They bore two children named Śūra and Parjanya. **Śūra produced Vasudeva** and others. Parjanya… became a vaiśya and worked with cows.»
- In Parjanya's assembly, Upananda gave Nanda the rule of Gokula «in that assembly with great souls like Vasudeva» (Pūrva-campū 3.31–32).
- **He sends Rohiṇī to Vraja** (Pūrva-campū 3.80): «Vasudeva, disturbed by uncontrollable Kaṃsa's anger, sent Rohiṇī, favorable to Vraja, to Vraja.» Balarāma's birth and name ceremony «were performed secretly on the advice of Vasudeva» (3.88), and for the naming of the boys «Vasudeva decided on highly qualified Garga, an ocean of austerity. Going to him alone, he requested Garga to make arrangements for his sons» (6.26).
- **Kṛṣṇa, son of Nanda and Vasudeva** (Pūrva-campū 3.102): «The four-armed form which appeared internally to Vasudeva and Devakī later appeared externally… Kṛṣṇa appeared always in a two-armed form to Nanda and Yaśodā.» Garga: «this beautiful son of yours sometimes appeared previously as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore, those who are learned sometimes call this child Vāsudeva» (SB 10.8.14).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 3.19, 3.31–32, 3.80, 3.88, 3.102, 6.26.

name: Sītā Ṭhākurāṇī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Yogamāyā** — in Vraja the ascetic **Paurṇamāsī**, «middle-aged» and dressed in red, who arranges all of Kṛṣṇa's pastimes with the gopīs.

## Gopāla-campū — Paurṇamāsī

- **Yogamāyā** (Pūrva-campū 2.28): «She who is famous as Yogamāyā among the assembly of siddhas, mentioned in Bhāgavatam by the words *yoga-māyām upāśritaḥ*, who is known as the svarūpa-śakti and controls the pastimes of the Lord, but who takes the form of an ascetic woman named Paurṇamāsī, then entered. All offered respects to her without pride and with reverence.»
- **Her coming to Vraja** (Pūrva-campū 3.71–79): before Kṛṣṇa's birth «an austere woman arrived with a brāhmaṇa boy… everyone… inquired, “You seem to be Yogamāyā personified. Who are you?”» — «“I am named Paurṇamāsī. I am middle-aged and wear red cloth. Since childhood I have performed austerities. I can see the future. This boy is Madhumaṅgala… We remain eternally at the age that you see us because of our special knowledge.”» She told them, «Nanda, your life and soul, will have a son who gives bliss to the universe», and they built her a hut by the Yamunā.
- **Guardian of the gopīs** (Pūrva-campū 15.40–69): Vṛndā came to her, «An austere woman named Paurṇamāsī, functioning as Yogamāyā, lived in a deep forest of Vṛndāvana», with the news that Kṛṣṇa's beloveds would be married to other men. «Paurṇamāsī said, “They will not get married to other men. I will prevent this by using my magical powers”» — «I have produced for all of them something like a bad dream in a waking state.» Then she consoled the young gopīs and led them secretly to Kṛṣṇa: «From that day, Viśākhā, Lalitā and others became the sakhīs of Rādhā» (verse 53).
- **The wedding** (Uttara-campū 31–35): her letter to Rādhā: «O Rādhā! You are named Rādhā. Your father is Vṛṣabhānu. Your mother is Kīrtidā. Yaśodā is your mother-in-law. Your friends are Lalitā and Viśākhā. The forests where Kṛṣṇa plays are your dwelling place. Kṛṣṇa is your husband at all times» (31, verse 45); «Paurṇamāsī has said, “I will accomplish everything in all places at once without obstruction”» (33.36–37); «Paurṇamāsī has spread the influence of Yogamāyā everywhere. Now the faultless auspiciousness of all the marriages of Kṛṣṇa will be described» (33.5). Leaving Vraja, Kṛṣṇa had told Madhumaṅgala: «serve Paurṇamāsī for my auspiciousness» (Uttara-campū 6.50).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Paurṇamāsī

Among the messengers: «Those messengers who, like Purṇamāsī, wear the cloth of renunciation are called liṅginī, ascetics» (Dūtī-bheda, text 4, p. 21).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 2.28, 3.71–79, 15.40–69 (verse 53); Uttara 6.50, 31.45, 33.5, 33.36–37; Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22).

name: Śrī Devī (wife of Advaita)
text:

name: Mukunda Sarakāra (Mukunda dāsa)
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Vṛndā-devī** (Vṛndārikā), the goddess of the forest of Vṛndāvana, one of Kṛṣṇa's three famous messengers, «one who speaks sweetly».

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Vṛndā

- **A messenger** (Dūtī-bheda, text 4): «vraje vīrā vṛndā vaṁśī ca kṛṣṇasya dūtī-trayam | … vṛndā ca priya-vādinī» — «In Vraja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa has three famous messengers: Vīrā, Vṛndā and Vaṁśī… Vṛndā is priya-vādinī (one who speaks sweetly).» «Vṛndā-devī, the presiding goddess of Vṛndāvana, is known as a vana-devī, forest goddess» (pp. 21–22).
- **A sakhī** (Sakhī-bheda, text 5): «yā kṛṣṇe snehādhikā sā sakhī | vṛndā, kundalatā, vidyā, dhaniṣṭhā, kusumikā tathā kāmadā nāmātreyī sakhī-bhāva-viśeṣa-bhāk» — «Sakhīs [the first category above] have more affection for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Examples are Vṛndā, Kundalatā, Vidhyā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Kusumikā, Kāmadā and Ātreyī» (p. 24).

## Gopāla-campū — Vṛndā

- **Who she is** (Pūrva-campū 15.40): «A certain woman would go to her [Paurṇamāsī] almost every day and night for consultation. One could not discern whether she was a devatā or human. She desired to act favorably for Kṛṣṇa's pastimes while protecting Vṛndāvana. She was a creeper of affection for Rādhā and other gopīs. **Her name was Vṛndārikā but was called Vṛndā for short.**»
- **Her fear for the gopīs** (Pūrva-campū 15.41–69): «Vṛndā said, “Oh! All of Kṛṣṇa's beloved gopīs are going to be married to other men.”» Paurṇamāsī promised to prevent it; «Vṛndā, falling at her feet with joy, began to weep in bliss.» When the weddings came near, «with pale face she went quickly to Paurṇamāsī and stood there like a clay doll», until Paurṇamāsī told her the secret: «I have produced for all of them something like a bad dream in a waking state.»
- **At the wedding**: «Vṛndā and Madhumaṅgala felt good» (Uttara-campū 30.32); with Madhumaṅgala she supported and served Paurṇamāsī (31.40, 32.19); the gopīs feel shy «in front of the devatā Vṛndā and the brāhmaṇa Madhumaṅgala» (36.41).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22), Sakhī-bheda 5 (pp. 23–24); Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.40–69; Uttara 30.32, 31.40, 32.19, 36.41.

name: Nīlāmbara Cakravartī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Garga Muni**, the sage who named Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma — and **Sumukha**, the chief cowherd who gave his daughter Yaśodā to Nanda.

## Gopāla-campū — Sumukha

«Then one of the chief cowherds named Sumukha gave his daughter to Nanda. That daughter controlled all relatives by her good qualities and bestowed abundant qualities to those who heard about her. Those who saw her increased their good qualities» (Pūrva-campū 3.30).

## Gopāla-campū — Garga

- He was in Parjanya's assembly when the family was handed to Upananda: «in the assembly attended by kings like Vasudeva and Garga» (Pūrva-campū 3.31).
- **The naming** (Pūrva-campū 6.26–32): «Vasudeva decided on highly qualified Garga, an ocean of austerity. Going to him alone, he requested Garga to make arrangements for his sons.» On the hundredth day «Garga, the most knowledgeable guru, the best of all sages, with speech like the Sāma Veda, arrived»; he had worshipped from childhood «a śālagrāma called Lakṣmī-nārāyaṇa». «Nanda had desired for a long time that Garga come to Vraja… He worshiped Garga shining like Brahman.» Garga saw Nanda «like the rising moon, not too old, with dazzling face and eyes… solidly built, tall, with long arms» (verse 18).
- **His words** (Pūrva-campū 3.102): «For many reasons, this beautiful son of yours sometimes appeared previously as the son of Vasudeva. Therefore, those who are learned sometimes call this child Vāsudeva» (SB 10.8.14).
- **He delays the betrothals** (Pūrva-campū 15.25–27): when the cowherds wanted to betroth their daughters to Kṛṣṇa, «omniscient Garga thought he should prevent this, after considering the advice of Vasudeva (to keep Kṛṣṇa's presence in Vraja secret)… “When Kṛṣṇa returns after killing Dantavakra, then all conditions will be perfect for marriage.”» He went to Paurṇamāsī to tell her.

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 3.30–31, 3.102, 6.26–32 (verse 18), 15.25–27.

name: Upendra Miśra
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Parjanya**, Nanda's father, son of Devamiḍha: the cowherd «like a cloud showering rain», who gave the world five sons and retired to Vṛndāvana to worship Govinda.

## Gopāla-campū — Parjanya

- **Parjanya** (Pūrva-campū 3.19): «Devamiḍha, who personified all the best qualities of the Yadu dynasty… lived in Mathurā. The best of kṣatriyas had two wives. One was of kṣatriya family and the other was of vaiśya family. They bore two children named Śūra and Parjanya. Śūra produced Vasudeva and others. Parjanya, because of his mixed parentage became a vaiśya and worked with cows. He lived in Mahāvana. From his childhood Parjanya would worship the brāhmaṇas just on seeing them and gave them everything to fulfill their desires. He was affectionate to them as Vaiṣṇavas… and worshiped Viṣṇu his whole» life.
- **Like a rain cloud** (3.23–24, verses 12–15): «It is not surprising that Parjanya surpassed the normal vaiśya by his conduct and wealth… He became the most prominent and was like a cloud showering rain.» «A rain cloud is one thing but Parjanya (meaning cloud) is a cloud of joy because he gave joy to the world by bestowing five sons starting with Upananda.» «Giving the sons the names Upananda, Abhinanda, Nanda, Sannanda and Nandana, he brought bliss (ānanda = nanda) under control.»
- **He retires to Vṛndāvana** (3.31–33, 3.43–44): «Parjanya gave bliss to all beings. He was without lamentation and possessed more wealth than others… He decided that he would spend his whole life in worshiping the lotus feet of Govinda.» He handed the family to Upananda, the eldest, «in the assembly attended by kings like Vasudeva and Garga», and Upananda by tilaka gave Nanda sovereignty over Gokula. «Then fortunate Parjanya entered Vṛndāvana to worship Govinda's lotus feet» — and to his son, who asked for the essence of all scriptures, he taught in brief: «Kṛṣṇa prema is happiness» (verse 19). «When excellent Parjanya went to Vṛndāvana with his excellent wife…» (3.44).
- **In Goloka** (Pūrva-campū 33.350): «at the assembly giving glory to Goloka, Parjanya, the best of all people, giving happiness to all his people, was seated among the respectable members in pure dress, showering all happiness like a cloud. **His excellent wife Varīyasī** shone in the gathering in the inner chambers.» And when the cowherds are brought back from Brahma-hrada «They will see Parjanya and others who had previously disappeared and become astonished» (Pūrva-campū 33, verse 120).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 3.19–44 (verses 12–19), 33.120, 33.350.

name: Kalāvatī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Varīyasī**, Parjanya's wife, Nanda's mother.

## Gopāla-campū — Varīyasī and Parjanya

The Gopāla-campū names her once: in Goloka «His excellent wife Varīyasī shone in the gathering in the inner chambers» (Pūrva-campū 33.350); «When excellent Parjanya went to Vṛndāvana with his excellent wife…» (3.44). Of her husband's family:

- **Parjanya** (Pūrva-campū 3.19): «Devamiḍha, who personified all the best qualities of the Yadu dynasty… lived in Mathurā. The best of kṣatriyas had two wives. One was of kṣatriya family and the other was of vaiśya family. They bore two children named Śūra and Parjanya. Śūra produced Vasudeva and others. Parjanya, because of his mixed parentage became a vaiśya and worked with cows. He lived in Mahāvana. From his childhood Parjanya would worship the brāhmaṇas just on seeing them and gave them everything to fulfill their desires. He was affectionate to them as Vaiṣṇavas… and worshiped Viṣṇu his whole» life.
- **Like a rain cloud** (3.23–24, verses 12–15): «It is not surprising that Parjanya surpassed the normal vaiśya by his conduct and wealth… He became the most prominent and was like a cloud showering rain.» «A rain cloud is one thing but Parjanya (meaning cloud) is a cloud of joy because he gave joy to the world by bestowing five sons starting with Upananda.» «Giving the sons the names Upananda, Abhinanda, Nanda, Sannanda and Nandana, he brought bliss (ānanda = nanda) under control.»
- **He retires to Vṛndāvana** (3.31–33, 3.43–44): «Parjanya gave bliss to all beings. He was without lamentation and possessed more wealth than others… He decided that he would spend his whole life in worshiping the lotus feet of Govinda.» He handed the family to Upananda, the eldest, «in the assembly attended by kings like Vasudeva and Garga», and Upananda by tilaka gave Nanda sovereignty over Gokula. «Then fortunate Parjanya entered Vṛndāvana to worship Govinda's lotus feet» — and to his son, who asked for the essence of all scriptures, he taught in brief: «Kṛṣṇa prema is happiness» (verse 19). «When excellent Parjanya went to Vṛndāvana with his excellent wife…» (3.44).
- **In Goloka** (Pūrva-campū 33.350): «at the assembly giving glory to Goloka, Parjanya, the best of all people, giving happiness to all his people, was seated among the respectable members in pure dress, showering all happiness like a cloud. **His excellent wife Varīyasī** shone in the gathering in the inner chambers.» And when the cowherds are brought back from Brahma-hrada «They will see Parjanya and others who had previously disappeared and become astonished» (Pūrva-campū 33, verse 120).

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 3.19–44 (verses 12–19), 33.120, 33.350.

name: Mādhava Miśra (father of Gadādhara)
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Vṛṣabhānu**, Śrī Rādhā's father, «a great cowherd… of good family and great wealth» (the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā makes Mādhava Miśra a special manifestation of him); his wife **Kīrtidā** was Ratnāvatī.

## Gopāla-campū — Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā

- **Rādhā's birth** (Pūrva-campū 15.16–18, verse 6): «Rādhā accepted birth in the ocean of a great cowherd named Vṛṣabhānu of good family and great wealth.» «The milk ocean of Vṛṣabhānu was a mine of gems in the form of his many sons but became perfect in producing nectar through the birth of Rādhā.» «She took birth when the moon was in Anurādhā constellation, bringing joy to all, one year after the birth of Kṛṣṇa.»
- «O Rādhā, giving fame to Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā!» (Uttara-campū 1.52); «Your father is Vṛṣabhānu. Your mother is Kīrtidā» (31, verse 45).
- **His family** (Uttara-campū 32.84): Madhumaṅgala, joking before the wedding: «Vṛṣabhānu and others, coming from an ambaṣṭha mother and the best of brāhmaṇa as a father, are called vaiśya abhīras… Vṛṣabhānu's grandfather's sister's husband gave his daughter to Devamīḍa, best of the Yadus.»
- **Giving Rādhā to Kṛṣṇa** (Uttara-campū 35): Vṛṣabhānu «performed the necessary Nāndīmukha» rites (35.8); «Before Kṛṣṇa had gone to Mathurā, Vṛṣabhānu had seen him hundreds of» times, but «Vṛṣabhānu saw him now, he appeared to be new. He stood motionless» (verse 23); «Vṛṣabhānu offered Kṛṣṇa two pieces of fine cloth, a sacred thread, and shoes» (verse 27). «Vṛṣabhānu, with tears in his eyes, with his trembling, damp hand took Rādhā's trembling hand and offered it to Kṛṣṇa's trembling hand» (verse 36).
- **His tears** (Uttara-campū 35, verse 60 and 35.37–39): «People knew that whatever Vṛṣabhānu and his wife spoke with broken words and tearful eyes was caused by giving away their daughter. But people did not know of the grief caused when they had previously given her to Abhimanyu.» «Righteous Vṛṣabhānu brought Kṛṣṇa into his house… and taking him by the hand spoke with Kīrtidā. Addressing him as his son, he spoke with tears in his eyes, “From her childhood my Rādhā has acted lifeless. Do not become angry at my fault.”» He «again offered his daughter, and then even his son Śrīdāma. Then with a painful heart he let the bride and groom leave.»

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.16–18; Uttara 1.52, 31.45, 32.84, 35.8–39 (verses 23–60).

name: Śrīla Puṇḍarīka Vidyānidhi
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Vṛṣabhānu**, Śrī Rādhā's father, «a great cowherd… of good family and great wealth».

## Gopāla-campū — Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā

- **Rādhā's birth** (Pūrva-campū 15.16–18, verse 6): «Rādhā accepted birth in the ocean of a great cowherd named Vṛṣabhānu of good family and great wealth.» «The milk ocean of Vṛṣabhānu was a mine of gems in the form of his many sons but became perfect in producing nectar through the birth of Rādhā.» «She took birth when the moon was in Anurādhā constellation, bringing joy to all, one year after the birth of Kṛṣṇa.»
- «O Rādhā, giving fame to Vṛṣabhānu and Kīrtidā!» (Uttara-campū 1.52); «Your father is Vṛṣabhānu. Your mother is Kīrtidā» (31, verse 45).
- **His family** (Uttara-campū 32.84): Madhumaṅgala, joking before the wedding: «Vṛṣabhānu and others, coming from an ambaṣṭha mother and the best of brāhmaṇa as a father, are called vaiśya abhīras… Vṛṣabhānu's grandfather's sister's husband gave his daughter to Devamīḍa, best of the Yadus.»
- **Giving Rādhā to Kṛṣṇa** (Uttara-campū 35): Vṛṣabhānu «performed the necessary Nāndīmukha» rites (35.8); «Before Kṛṣṇa had gone to Mathurā, Vṛṣabhānu had seen him hundreds of» times, but «Vṛṣabhānu saw him now, he appeared to be new. He stood motionless» (verse 23); «Vṛṣabhānu offered Kṛṣṇa two pieces of fine cloth, a sacred thread, and shoes» (verse 27). «Vṛṣabhānu, with tears in his eyes, with his trembling, damp hand took Rādhā's trembling hand and offered it to Kṛṣṇa's trembling hand» (verse 36).
- **His tears** (Uttara-campū 35, verse 60 and 35.37–39): «People knew that whatever Vṛṣabhānu and his wife spoke with broken words and tearful eyes was caused by giving away their daughter. But people did not know of the grief caused when they had previously given her to Abhimanyu.» «Righteous Vṛṣabhānu brought Kṛṣṇa into his house… and taking him by the hand spoke with Kīrtidā. Addressing him as his son, he spoke with tears in his eyes, “From her childhood my Rādhā has acted lifeless. Do not become angry at my fault.”» He «again offered his daughter, and then even his son Śrīdāma. Then with a painful heart he let the bride and groom leave.»

## Sources

Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.16–18; Uttara 1.52, 31.45, 32.84, 35.8–39 (verses 23–60).

name: Śaṅkara Paṇḍit
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Śrībhadrā** — the books speak of **Bhadrā**, one of the eight principal heroines of Vraja, neutral to Śrī Rādhā, gentle, dressed in many colours. (They do not say if she is the same as the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā's Śrībhadrā.)

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Bhadrā

> śrī-rādhāyāḥ … taṭastha-pakṣaḥ bhadrā … bhadrā dakṣiṇā mṛdvī citra-vasanā (Nāyikā-svabhāva, text 3)

- «Bhadrā Sakhī is taṭasthā-pakṣa, meaning she is neutral towards Śrīmatī Rādhikā» (p. 19). «Bhadrā is dakṣiṇā and mṛdvī and wears cloth of many different colours» (pp. 20–21).
- She is *dhīrā-pragalbhā*: «The heroines who conceal their anger and display indifference to Kṛṣṇa's embraces are called dhīrā-pragalbhā. In Vraja, Candrāvalī, Pālikā and Bhadrā are examples» (p. 12).
- **Her love** (Rati-bheda): «When nīlī-rāga is perfected after a long time… it is called śyāma-rāga. Śyāma-rāga is present in Bhadrā and gopīs following her» (p. 40).

## Gopāla-campū — Bhadrā

- **In the rāsa** (Pūrva-campū 25, verse 29): «Seeing Govinda approaching one gopī, overjoyed, said, “Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa!” She said nothing else» (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.13.43) — «That gopī was Bhadrā.»
- «Bhadrā, Padmā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Śaibya, Pālikā, Śyāmalā and Candrāvalī have surpassed Lakṣmī» (Pūrva-campū 15, verse 32); Kṛṣṇa: «I always go to Bhadrā and Padmā» (21.110).
- **One of the eight heroines** (Uttara-campū 31.51): «O Rādhā, Candrāvalī, Lalitā, Viśākhā, Bhadrā, Śyāmā, Padmā, Śaibya!» — in separation, «Bhadrā is stunned in separation… The eight gopīs are afflicted by eight sāttvika-bhāvas» (36, verse 8).
- **In Dvārakā** (Uttara-campū 17, verse 53): «Bhadrāvalī was Bhadrā.»

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Nāyikā-vibhāga (p. 12), Nāyikā-svabhāva 3 (pp. 17–21), Rati-bheda (p. 40); Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.32, 21.110, 25.29; Uttara 17.53, 31.51, 36.8.

name: Śrī Rāghava Paṇḍita
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Dhaniṣṭhā**, a gopī of Vraja whose affection is greater for Kṛṣṇa — one of the *sakhīs* of the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi.

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — Dhaniṣṭhā

> yā kṛṣṇe snehādhikā sā sakhī | vṛndā, kundalatā, vidyā, dhaniṣṭhā, kusumikā tathā kāmadā nāmātreyī sakhī-bhāva-viśeṣa-bhāk (Sakhī-bheda, text 5)

«There are five different types of sakhīs: (1) sakhī, (2) nitya-sakhī, (3) prāṇa-sakhī, (4) priya-sakhī and (5) parama-preṣṭha-sakhī. Of these, some possess equal affection for both Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa (sama-sneha), while others are partial to either Śrī Rādhā or Śrī Kṛṣṇa (viṣama-sneha). **Sakhīs [the first category above] have more affection for Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Examples are Vṛndā, Kundalatā, Vidhyā, Dhaniṣṭhā, Kusumikā, Kāmadā and Ātreyī**» (pp. 23–24).

## Gopāla-campū — Dhaniṣṭhā

«Bhadrā, Padmā, **Dhaniṣṭhā**, Śaibya, Pālikā, Śyāmalā and Candrāvalī have surpassed Lakṣmī during this age» (Pūrva-campū 15, verse 32).

## Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa — the messengers of Vraja

> atha dūtī dvi-vidhā, svayaṁ dūti āpta-dūtī ca | tatrāpta-dūtī ca trividhāḥ, amitārthā nisṛṣṭārthā patra-hāriṇī ca | … tāḥ śilpa-kāriṇī daivajñā liṅginī paricārikā dhātreyī vanadevī sakhī cety ādayaḥ | vraje vīrā vṛndā vaṁśī ca kṛṣṇasya dūtī-trayam | pragalbha-vacanā vīrā vṛndā ca priya-vādinī, sarva-kārya-sādhikā vaṁśī (Dūtī-bheda, text 4)

- «A dūtī is defined as a sakhī who takes a message from the heroine to the hero, or vice versa. Svayaṁ-dūtī is the heroine herself, when she indicates to the hero the location of the meeting place. An āpta-dūtī is a follower who conveys the message.»
- «An amitārthā-dūtī acts as a messenger, although a verbal message is not conveyed to her. She simply comprehends an indication. A nisṛṣṭārthā-dūtī performs all services upon receiving a command and personally shoulders the total responsibility of arranging the meeting between Śrī Rādhā and Śrī Kṛṣṇa. A patra-hāriṇī is a messenger who carries letters and removes obstructions in the meeting of the hero and heroine.»
- «These messengers are artisans (śilpakāriṇī), fortune tellers (daivajñā), ascetics (liṅginī), servants (paricārikā), nurses (dhātreyī), forest goddesses (vana-devī), girlfriends (sakhī) and others… Those messengers who, like Purṇamāsī, wear the cloth of renunciation are called liṅginī… Sakhīs such as Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Bhānumatī Mañjarī are called paricārikā… Vṛndā-devī, the presiding goddess of Vṛndāvana, is known as a vana-devī… According to the necessity of the time, all sakhīs act as messengers.»
- «In Vraja, Śrī Kṛṣṇa has three famous messengers: Vīrā, Vṛndā and Vaṁśī. Vīrā is pragalbha-vacanā (a harsh speaker), Vṛndā is priya-vādinī (one who speaks sweetly), and Vaṁśī, Śrī Kṛṣṇa's flute, is sarva-kārya-sādhikā (one who accomplishes everything)» (pp. 20–22).

## Sources

Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa, Sakhī-bheda 5 (pp. 23–24), Dūtī-bheda 4 (pp. 20–22); Gopāla-campū, Pūrva 15.32.

name: Mālinī Ṭhākurāṇī
text:
## In the Vraja-nitya-līlā

**Ambikā**, Kṛṣṇa's nurse in Vraja.

The Gopāla-campū and the Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi-kiraṇa do not name Kṛṣṇa's nurse Ambikā (the Gopāla-campū's «Ambikā forest», where the people of Vraja went to worship Śiva, is a place).
